Neugebauer, the co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has issued a statement in response to the company's decision to drop its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment. The lawsuit's dismissal comes after a Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw amendment, and Neugebauer claims that the company's actions confirm that the bylaw move was about entrenching the board's power rather than good governance. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

general.title: US Jobs Report Could Offer Clues on Workforce Participation Drop
general.summary: A recent plunge in US labor force participation has sparked competing theories about whether persistent drivers — like aging and immigration — or more temporary seasonal shifts are to blame. Any evidence in upcoming jobs reports could reshape how policymakers view the labor market.

general.summary: Bank of Japan accounts showed no sign of a major intervention in the currency market by Tokyo on Wednesday, suggesting that sharp moves in the exchange rate that day were likely driven by twitchy traders amid a re-calibration of rate hike expectations.

general.summary: Martin Blessing, who is German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s personal representative for investments, discusses the economy, banking consolidation and the surge in energy costs ahead of the European winter. Blessing, the former CEO of Commerzbank AG, speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
